relevance.rationale: String-theory paper showing that most four-dimensional CHL models are self-dual under a weak-strong duality acting on the heterotic axio-dilaton by the Fricke involution S -> -1/(NS), and that self-duality is equivalent to N-modularity of the electric charge lattice (isometric to its dual up to rescaling of the quadratic form by N). The corpus has an active Fricke arc: the tau-dictionary work uses the Fricke involution W_5 on Gamma_0(5) and enumerates a 'bar <-> Fricke' candidate class in which the bar involution q -> q^{-1} would correspond to W_5. That arc's own audit records that every enumerated candidate FAILS the hauptmodul gate -- the candidates were enumerated from structure but selected by nothing. This document is worth citing because it supplies exactly the missing shape: a structural criterion (N-modularity of a lattice) under which a Fricke involution IS a strong-weak duality, rather than a list of candidates. It is NOT load-bearing and I will not claim it rescues the failed gate: the criterion's hypotheses concern the electric-magnetic charge lattice of a CHL compactification, an object with no established counterpart in this corpus, so the criterion cannot be applied today. It is context that tells the reader Fricke self-duality has a known lattice characterisation, not a tool the corpus can pick up. A separate hazard worth recording: 'Fricke' already means the Fricke TRACE identity for SL(2) character varieties in prop:chirality-from-frobenius-self-pairing and conj:depth-stratified-frobenius-reciprocity -- a different object from the Fricke involution, and any citation must say which.

keyResults.statement: A CHL model is self-dual under the Fricke involution S -> -1/(NS) if and only if its lattice of purely electric charges is N-modular, i.e. isometric to its dual after rescaling the quadratic form by N.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the form a structural selection principle for the corpus's bar <-> Fricke identification would take -- a lattice condition rather than a numerical gate -- which is what the enumerated-and-failed candidate class currently lacks.

proposedActions.rationale: The corpus's Fricke-involution work has no bibliographic anchor for the involution's role as a strong-weak duality; the entry would also let the two distinct 'Fricke' objects be disambiguated in one place.

A short remark distinguishing the Fricke TRACE identity (already used in the mass-theory blocks) from the Fricke INVOLUTION W_N (used in the tau-dictionary audits), and noting that self-duality under the latter has a known lattice characterisation, would close a live symbol collision.
